items.title: Testing human ability to detect ‘deepfake’ images of human faces

judge.evidence_empirical: Using an online survey, participants (N = 280) were randomly allocated to one of four groups: a control group, and three assistance interventions.

items.title: AI Hyperrealism: Why AI Faces Are Perceived as More Real Than Human Ones

judge.evidence_topic: In Experiment 1 ( N = 124 adults), alongside our reanalysis of previously published data, we showed that White AI faces are judged as human more often than actual human faces—a phenomenon we term AI hyperrealism.
judge.evidence_empirical: In Experiment 1 ( N = 124 adults)... In Experiment 2 ( N = 610 adults)...

items.title: Training human super-recognizers’ detection and discrimination of AI-generated faces

judge.evidence_topic: Here, we investigate synthetic face detection and discrimination in super-recognizers (SRs; who have exceptional face recognition skills), and typical-ability control participants.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two different experimental designs, we found that SRs (total N = 283) were better at detecting and discriminating synthetic faces than controls (total N = 381)
judge.reason: O artigo atende aos critérios de tema e empirismo. O achado principal está correto e sustentado pelo resumo. Contudo, o tamanho da amostra extraído está incompleto, pois omite o número de participantes do grupo controle (N=381), citando apenas o grupo de super-reconhecedores (N=283).

items.title: AI-generated images of familiar faces are indistinguishable from real photographs

judge.evidence_topic: Here, we investigated a new method for generating face images (via ChatGPT plus DALL·E) and its application to both fictional and real (in this case, celebrity) identities.
judge.evidence_empirical: Our results demonstrated that generated images of both fictional (Experiment 1) and celebrity identities (Experiment 2) could not be distinguished from real photographs.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico com quatro experimentos envolvendo participantes humanos para avaliar a percepção de imagens sintéticas. O tema está dentro do escopo, não trata de política ou saúde, e o tamanho da amostra não consta no resumo, conforme indicado.

items.title: A (Mid)journey Through Reality: Assessing Accuracy, Impostor Bias, and Automation Bias in Human Detection of AI‐Generated Images

judge.evidence_topic: This study addresses this gap by providing the first quantitative analysis of how these two biases operate across five distinct experimental variants designed to test the context‐dependency of human perception.

items.title: Deepfake smiles matter less—the psychological and neural impact of presumed AI-generated faces

judge.evidence_topic: Here we investigate the impact of the belief that depicted persons are real or deepfakes on psychological and neural measures of human face perception.
judge.evidence_empirical: Using EEG, we tracked participants’ (N = 30) brain responses to real faces showing positive, neutral, and negative expressions, after being informed that they are either real or fake.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico com participantes humanos que investiga a percepção de rostos sintéticos, alinhando-se ao tema. O método (EEG e avaliações) está correto e o achado principal é sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Deciphering authenticity in the age of AI: how AI-generated disinformation images and AI detection tools influence judgements of authenticity

judge.evidence_topic: This experimental study explored how aesthetic realism and emotional salience, as key features of both AI-generated content and disinformation, may influence authenticity judgements of AI-generated disinformation images.
judge.evidence_empirical: In this study, 292 UK-based participants were presented with both AI-generated and non-AI-generated disinformation images which varied in aesthetic realism and emotional salience.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico com participantes humanos sobre a percepção de imagens geradas por IA. O foco é o realismo estético e a saliência emocional, não sendo um estudo centrado em políticos ou eleições, apesar da menção ao contexto de desinformação. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Crowds Improve Human Detection of <scp>AI</scp>‐Synthesised Faces

judge.evidence_topic: Artificial intelligence can now synthesise face images which people cannot distinguish from real faces. Here, we investigated the wisdom of the (outer) crowd (averaging individuals' responses to the same trial) and inner crowd (averaging the same individual's responses to the same trial after completing the test twice) as routes to increased performance.
judge.evidence_empirical: In Experiment 1, participants viewed synthetic and real faces, and rated whether they thought each face was synthetic or real using a 1–7 scale. ... In Experiment 2, participants judged each face only once, providing a binary ‘synthetic/real’ response
judge.reason: O artigo descreve dois experimentos com participantes humanos para avaliar a detecção de rostos sintéticos, alinhando-se ao pedido. Os achados extraídos refletem precisamente as conclusões apresentadas no resumo e o tamanho da amostra não é mencionado no texto fornecido.

items.title: Examining the role of compression in influencing AI-generated image authenticity

judge.evidence_topic: In this paper, we systematically study this problem by creating the first-ever AIGC image dataset for subjective evaluations of authenticity discrimination.

judge.reason: O artigo descreve um estudo empírico com participantes humanos para avaliar a autenticidade de imagens geradas por IA, conforme solicitado. O achado principal está explicitamente presente no resumo.

items.title: Partial Fake Speech Attacks in the Real World Using Deepfake Audio

judge.evidence_topic: This paper studies how well humans and machines, including speaker recognition systems and existing fake-speech detection tools, can distinguish between human voice and computer-generated speech.
judge.evidence_empirical: Our study shows that both humans and machines can be easily deceived by PF speech, and the current defences against PF speech are insufficient.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico publicado em 2025 que investiga a percepção humana de áudio sintético (deepfake), atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. Os dados extraídos refletem corretamente o conteúdo do resumo.
